newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada's Goodale to state CWB changes in 1-2 weeks.
newsitem.headline: Canada's Goodale to state CWB changes in 1-2 weeks.

text.p: Canadian Agriculture Minister Ralph Goodale said on Saturday he plans to announce the changes he wants for the Canadian Wheat Board within 14 days.
"I hope that within a week or two to be able to put out a comprehensive response," Goodale told reporters after a speech to the Canadian Farm Writers' annual conference here.
Goodale appointed a federal export review panel in late 1995 to study commodity marketing on the Prairies.
It made sweeping recommendations in July, including revamping the way the CWB is run and what it sells.

The 61-year-old state commodity trading agency, one of the world's oldest and largest, has been under increasing fire since last fall when spot prices in wheat at U.S. border elevators outstripped the CWB's monthly price estimates.

After the panel proposals were unveiled, one farm protest group stopped its regular border runs to truck wheat and barley to U.S. elevators without the legally required CWB export permit until Goodale rules on the recommendations.
Goodale declined to say which proposals he'd discarded but he said there seemed to be agreement on a plan to have a board of directors and a chief executive at the CWB.
It is now run by three federally appointed commissioners.
"By and large, while there's some argument about nuance and detail, the general thrust of those recommendations appear to have a broad body of support from all sides," Goodale said.

The industry appeared evenly split and bitterly divided on other recommendations such as removing the CWB's export monopoly on feed barley or pricing a quarter of the wheat crop on a proposed CWB spot market.

A survey commissioned by Goodale's department showed 47 percent of the 760 farmers questioned favoured the suggestion they be able to price part of their wheat crop at a spot price offered by the CWB but outside the CWB pool account while 43 percent opposed the suggestion.
Twenty five percent of farmers strongly opposed the proposal while 13 percent strongly supported it.

While 55 percent approved taking feed barley out of the CWB's exclusive marketing jurisdiction, 27 percent of respondents strongly supported removing feed barley from the CWB monopoly while 28 percent strongly opposed such a move.
"In a dual (non-monopoly) market, the Canadian Wheat Board would be diminished, it could not guarantee quantity, neither could it guarantee quality," Goodale said.

The CWB held a 21 percent share of the world's bread wheat market in the year ended July 31, 1995, selling 13.73 million tonnes to 70 nations and supplying half of China's import needs, the single largest in the world.

Whether one grain firm should have exclusive access to all wheat, durum, feed and malting barley grown on Canada's Prairies has become so divisive that Alberta's government placed radio ads this week calling for an end to the CWB monopoly.
The Alberta Barley Commission plans a constitutional challenge to the CWB's mandatory monopoly on grain sourcing next month.
Meanwhile, Saskatchewan's government fired back stating the agency maximizes returns to producers in Canada's largest agricultural province.

Thirty two percent of farmers interviewed during the 10 -minute phone poll said they would like to see "a major overhaul" of the CWB. Thirty six percent of farmers said they would like to see "minor improvements" to the CWB.
Three percent favoured "completely eliminating" the CWB.
"The more contentious issues fall within the (CWB) jurisdiction and those are the recommendations that will require the most careful judgement," Goodale said.
-- Winnipeg bureau 204 947 3548
